Vinod S. Bhardwaj, J. (Oral)
Prayer in the application is for condonation of delay of 18 days in filing the appeal.
For the reasons mentioned in the application, the same is allowed and delay of 18 days in filing the appeal is condoned.
Application is allowed as prayed for.

The present application has been preferred under Section 378(4) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter 'CR.P.C.') seeking grant of leave to appeal against the judgment of acquittal dated 04.12.2023 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class Hisar in a case stemming from criminal complaint dated 23.07.2016 filed under Sections 177, 200, 406, 420 & 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.
1 of 2
After assessing all the material available on the record, the learned trial Court acquitted the respondent(s) vide judgment dated 04.12.2023.

3. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the applicant submits that in view of the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in M/s. Celestium Financial vs. A. Gnanasekaran Etc., 2025(3) RCR Ram Kumar vs Santosh on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33853350/
1 (Criminal) 208, the applicant would have a remedy before the Court of Sessions.
4. In view of the judgment rendered by the Apex Court in Celestium Financial (supra), the present application seeking leave to appeal is remanded to the learned Sessions Judge, Hisar with a direction to treat the same as an appeal filed under Section 372 of the Cr.P.C. (now Section 413 of BNSS) and entrust the same to appropriate Court for its disposal on merits.
5.
